Member
mĕm´bĕr
n. (a limb or organ of a body; a constituent part of a whole; rendering Greek melos)
From Latin membrum, a limb. Paul's ecclesiology is built on this word: the church is not an association of individuals but a body of members.

Biblical Definition

A member is a limb or organ — a part that has no life apart from the body it belongs to. Paul makes it the governing image of the church: “whether one member suffer, all the members suffer with it; or one member be honoured, all the members rejoice with it” (1Co 12:26). Membership on this definition is not a club roll but an organic union in which another Christian's pain is felt in one's own body. The same word governs the doctrine of the body's holiness: “Know ye not that your bodies are the members of Christ? shall I then take the members of Christ, and make them the members of an harlot? God forbid” (1Co 6:15) — sexual sin is not merely rule-breaking but the dragging of Christ's own limbs into a union that dishonours Him. And James applies it to the smallest organ: “Even so the tongue is a little member, and boasteth great things. Behold, how great a matter a little fire kindleth!” (Jas 3:5). A member is small, joined, and consequential — which is the whole doctrine of the local church in three words.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines member as a limb of an animal body, a part of a whole, and one of a community or society — the sense Paul gives the church.

expand to see more

MEMBER, n. A limb of animal bodies; as a leg, an arm, an ear.

2. A part of a discourse, or of a period or sentence.

3. Any part of an integral.

4. A part of a community or society; as, every citizen is a member of the state.

5. In Scripture, a believer, as a part of the body of Christ.

Key Scripture

1Co 12:26 — "And whether one member suffer, all the members suffer with it; or one member be honoured, all the members rejoice with it."

1Co 6:15 — "Know ye not that your bodies are the members of Christ? shall I then take the members of Christ, and make them the members of an harlot? God forbid."

Jas 3:5 — "Even so the tongue is a little member, and boasteth great things. Behold, how great a matter a little fire kindleth!"

1Pe 2:9 — "But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light:"

Modern Corruption

Church membership has been reduced to attendance, preference, or a name on a database, so that the very thing Paul used the word to exclude — a Christianity of detached individuals — is now the ordinary practice.

expand to see more

The consumer model of church treats the congregation as a service provider and the Christian as a customer who may sample, switch, or absent himself without injury to anyone. Paul's word forbids it. A hand does not attend the body on weeks when it finds the body edifying; it is joined, and its detachment is an amputation. This is why the New Testament assumes a definable congregation with known members and real elders — a body cannot suffer with a member it cannot identify, and church discipline is unintelligible without a roll it means something to be on.

1 Corinthians 6 shows the doctrine reaching into the body. Because the believer's limbs are Christ's members, what is done with them is done with His. That single premise settles more sexual ethics than any list of prohibitions, and it explains why Paul answers the Corinthian slogan about liberty not with a rule but with a fact of union. James then reminds us that the smallest member sets the largest fires, so that the tongue — gossip, slander, the whispered comparison — is precisely where the health of a body is decided.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek melos (G3196), a limb or member of the body — used of the believer's own limbs, of Christians in the church, and of the church in Christ.

expand to see more

Greek melos (G3196) — a limb, member; “whether one member suffer” (1Co 12:26).

The same word in Rom 6:13 — yield your members as instruments of righteousness unto God — makes the limbs the battleground of sanctification.

In Eph 5:30 believers are members of His body, of His flesh, and of His bones — the union grounded in marriage language.

Usage

"“Whether one member suffer, all the members suffer with it” — membership defined by shared pain."

"“Your bodies are the members of Christ” — the premise behind Christian sexual ethics."

"“The tongue is a little member, and boasteth great things” — the smallest limb, the largest fire."
